A year later, the sheep’s tongue gradually withered and shrank away. He submitted a petition to resign from his official post. County Magistrate Zheng Yuping suspected this was a deception and ordered him to open his mouth to verify it;
seeing that only a portion of the tongue root, about the size of a bean, remained, he asked for the reason. The man took paper and wrote a response. The County...
He ordered [the man] to copy the *Lotus Sūtra* to accrue merit for the sheep. As predicted, the man resolved his mind to transcribe it; he observed the precepts and fasts without slackening.

After one year, his tongue gradually began to grow back and was restored to its former state. He then went to the local government office to submit a petition, and the magistrate appointed him as the village head (*li-zheng*).

Cui Yiqi, the Junior Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments during the Tang dynasty, was the father-in-law of Xiao Wenkeng, who had long maintained the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*, reciting it over several thousand times and permanently abstaining from pungent vegetables and meat.
His wife, Lady Xiao, passed away in the fifth month of the third year of the Longshuo era; on the twenty-first day (the third seven-day period), a vegetarian feast (*zhāi*) was held.
The maidservant Suyu suddenly spoke in the manner of a noble lady, saying: "In life, I did not believe in the Triple Gem; now I suffer unspeakable pain.
Because you have recited sutras and performed vegetarian feasts for me, I have been granted temporary release.
Return on the twentieth day and come again to take me away, so that I may see my own suffering. When the appointed time arrived, Suyu indeed died; three days later, she revived and said: "I saw..."
In the palace of the great city, the lady entered a separate courtyard. In an instant, cauldrons of fire and iron beds arrived together; she underwent every form of bitter torment.
Suddenly, she saw Keng seated upon a lotus pedestal, who said to Suyu: "My daughter, you were full of anger and jealousy;
you did not believe my words, nor did you believe in cause and effect. Now you undergo this suffering, and I am unable to save you. When you return home, you may tell your family."
He was thus led to cultivate merit, hoping thereby to attain liberation. Furthermore, he saw a Brahman monk descend from the air, instructing him to recite the Lotus Sūtra.
The monk said to him, "You must memorize this sūtra and transmit it for the people of Jambudvīpa; there shall surely be those who believe.

In the first month of the first year of the Linde era, a vegetarian feast was prepared at the residence of General Xue to welcome Daoyu, who was then tested on his recitation of the *Mingjing* (Sūtra of the Netherworld). There was...
When the Indian monks heard this, they joined their palms and sighed in admiration, saying, "It is no different from our own land in the West. The assembly was then struck with wonder and reverence.

As for the "Horse-riding Wife" of Tang, she originated from the region west of Shanzhou. Previously, the local customs there had been those of horsemanship and archery, and the people were unaware even of the names of the Three Jewels.
In the twelfth year of the Yuanhe era, a beautiful and elegant woman suddenly appeared, carrying a basket to sell fish; the people vied with one another to buy it.
He sought to marry her. The girl said, "If there is one who can recite the *Samantamukha-parivarta* in a single night, then I shall become his wife.
At dawn, more than twenty people had mastered it. He then gave them the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā*, and by morning, only about ten had mastered it.

He then gave them the complete text of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* and set a deadline of three days for full mastery. Only the son of the Ma family was able to achieve this; thus, he prepared the formal marriage rites.

They went out to welcome him. Upon entering the gate, the woman feigned illness and requested to stay in a separate room; shortly thereafter, she died, and her body immediately began to rot and decay. They then buried her.
A few days later, an elderly monk wearing purple robes arrived at the burial site and ordered the grave to be opened for inspection.

Inside, there remained only a skeleton with golden chain-like bones. He said to the assembly, "This is the Great Being Avalokiteśvara. Out of compassion for you all, who possess heavy karmic obstructions, he has manifested this skillful means."

"This was merely a manifestation to transform you. Having spoken these words, she flew through the air and departed. (According to one version of the Preface to the Portrait Eulogy by Song Qianxi, this refers to Puxian.
The two daughters of the Huang family of Tang were natives of Jinling. From their youth, they had heard others reciting the *Lotus Sūtra* and listened intently for a long time, after which they said:

"I have understood this meaning," she said, and was subsequently able to discourse deeply on the principles of the true mark (*bhūtalakṣaṇa*). Later, she entered the capital to reside at An-guo Temple as a nun;
her senior name was Chih-fa, and her junior name was Hui-jen. Together they practiced the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-samādhi*.

Suddenly, a nun named Kung-ku appeared, whose speech and appearance were most extraordinary. She descended to the place where they were performing repentance and joined them in their practice. Every time they reached midnight, her body would emit light.
It was magnificent. After remaining thus for three years, it departed. Some suspect it was a manifestation of Samantabhadra. This was recorded by Liang Su in the third year of the Xingyuan era.
During the Wude period of the Tang dynasty, Su Chang, the Director of Waterways, was appointed as the Prefect of Bazhou. While crossing the Jialing River at midstream—
A wind arose and the boat capsized; everyone fell into the water at once, except for one concubine who regularly recited the Lotus Sūtra.

When the water entered the boat, she placed the scripture case upon her head and vowed to perish with it. Thereupon, she alone did not sink, but floated along with the waves. After a short while, she reached the shore;
carrying the case, she stepped ashore and opened it to find that it was completely dry. The concubine survived unharmed. Furthermore—
To the north of Huaineng City, there were an aunt and her niece who recited the Lotus Sūtra together; their voices were like jade and gold.
After they passed away, a single red lotus grew from their tomb, blooming with exquisite beauty. Later, people built Huatai Temple on that site.
*Records of Miraculous Experiences from Successive Dynasties of Those Who Upheld the Lotus Sūtra*, Volume Upper;
*Records of Miraculous Experiences from Successive Dynasties of Those Who Upheld the Lotus Sūtra*, Volume Lower.
Compiled by the Daoist Zhou Kefu, with corrections by his son Zhou Shi.
The Recluse Qianque, Chen Jisheng, studied the case of a monk at Daci Temple in Chengdu during the Five Dynasties period who constantly recited the Lotus Sutra. One day, he entered Mount Qingcheng.

While gathering medicinal herbs, he followed a mountain stream and crossed perilous terrain. Suddenly, clouds and mist rose on all sides, and he lost his way. After a short while, the clouds dispersed, and he saw a pavilion spanning the stream, exceedingly lofty and magnificent.
A monk arrived at the gate, and a servant entered to announce him. The monk came out and said, "The Master requests that you recite the scripture you have mastered.

The monk recited it with a clear voice until they reached the "Jeweled Stupa" chapter (*Ratnakoṭi-parivarta*). At that moment, the Master appeared wearing rustic clothes and carrying a staff of sorrel wood; his two eyebrows...
His robes hung down to his shoulders. He burned incense and bowed as he listened for a long while. When the recitation was finished, he served millet rice with *qǐ* and chrysanthemum;
it was fragrant like nectar. He offered a reward of one *huán* of gold. As the servant escorted him halfway, the monk asked his name. The servant replied, "This is Master Sun Simiao.
Just as the monk was sighing in admiration, the servant suddenly vanished. The monk searched for him for three days, but ultimately lost his way back to his former location and returned home.

Upon examining what had been offered as a gift, he found it was gold and silver coins. From that single meal, his body became light and free from ailment. According to the *History of the Tang*, Huimiao lived for one hundred and fifty years;
by the time he requested to recite the scriptures, another three hundred years had passed since his previous record. This account is drawn from the *Records from the Wilds of Xiang*.
Shi Daohan of Yongming Temple in Qiantang, Wuyue, was a member of the Pujin Wu clan.
Once, while performing the *Saptāha* Lotus Repentance ritual in his mountain study, he suddenly saw Samantabhadra riding an elephant below the pavilion at the triple gate of the temple.

The elephant’s trunk stretched directly toward the place where he was performing the repentance. Later, Qian Wang, the ruler of the Southern Han state, established Huiji Yongming Temple and invited the Master to reside there.
He once perused the Tripitaka; while sitting in meditative equipoise, he beheld Mañjuśrī manifesting his form.

Later, when he prostrated before the Aśoka Stūpa, he knelt and placed it upon his head, and tears fell like rain. Suddenly, he saw the śarīra relics outside a suspended bell, circumambulating as they moved.
The Master was filled with a mixture of grief and joy. In the second year of the Jianlong era, he passed away while seated; his body was cremated, and the resulting śarīra were exceedingly numerous.
A stupa was erected to enshrine them, from the summit of which a white light radiated, just as it had at the time of his initial transformation.
The Chan Master Zhijue of Yongming Temple in Wuyue was named Yanshou. He was of the Wang clan from Danyang and later moved to Yuhang.
During his childhood, he could recite the Lotus Sūtra at a speed of seven lines at once, so moving that he inspired a flock of sheep to kneel and listen. At the age of twenty-eight, he...

He served as the military commander of Huating Town. Because he had used official funds to release living creatures, he was sentenced to death for his crime. At the moment of execution, his countenance remained unchanged.
King Wenmu found this extraordinary and released him, ordering him to enter the monastic life. He relied upon Master Cuiyan of Siming and resided at Longce Temple.
There, he performed manual labor to provide for the community, ate but one meal a day, and sat constantly without lying down. Before long, he visited National Teacher Shao of Tiantai.

The Master resided at Guoqing Temple and practiced the Lotus Repentance. In the middle of the night, he beheld Samantabhadra Bodhisattva holding a lotus flower, who suddenly placed it in the Master’s hand.
Furthermore, while practicing meditative concentration for ninety days on Mount Tiantai at Tianzhu Peak, he saw Avalokiteśvara Mahāsattva, who poured nectar over him;
thereupon, he attained unimpeded eloquence. In the second year of the Jianlong era, King Zhongyi invited him to reside at Yongming.
At the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), a monk asked: "The sutra says that all Buddhas and all Buddha-dharmas emerge from this sutra.
What is this sutra? The Master said: "Constantly revolving or not revolving; it is neither meaning nor sound. The monk asked: "How does one receive and uphold it? The Master said:
"If you wish to receive and uphold it, you must listen with your eyes open. He resided at Yongming for fifteen years. [The assembly...]

He regularly maintained two thousand disciples and was titled Zhijue. In the seventh year of the Kaibao era, he entered Mount Tiantai, where he conferred the precepts upon approximately ten thousand people.

He constantly bestowed the Bodhisattva precepts upon the seven classes of followers. At night he offered food to hungry ghosts; in the morning he released living beings; throughout the six periods of the day he scattered flowers and practiced the Way;
and daily he recited one hundred and eight items of scripture, never failing for even a moment. With his remaining strength, he recited the Lotus Sūtra, totaling ten thousand scrolls.
He compiled three thousand fascicles, all of which were dedicated toward the adornment of the Pure Land. At that time, he was known as Maitreya’s Descent.
He authored the *Zongjing lu* (Record of the Mirror of the Source) in one hundred fascicles to synthesize the differing and identical tenets of the Tiantai, Xianshou, and Cien schools.

He also composed the *Xin fu* (Poem on the Mind), the *Weixin jue* (Secret Instructions on Mind-Only), and the *Wanshan tonggui* (The Ten Thousand Good Deeds Return to One Source) and other records. Once, while traveling at night to another peak to practice the Way, he occasionally heard the sound of a conch shell in the air.

Accompanied by the sounds of celestial music, on the second month of the eighth year of the Kaibō era, at the age of ninety-eight, he entered nirvana while burning incense and sitting in the full lotus posture.
His stupa was enshrined at Mount Daisai. The King of the Netherworld painted his likeness and paid him homage, as detailed in a separate biography.
Shi Hongchu of Dayun Temple in Wenzhou, Wuyue, was the son of the Tang family of Yongjia. From birth, he possessed auspicious signs and naturally transcended the mundane world.
At the beginning of the Qianhua era, Qian Wusuku invited the Master to reside at Longxing Temple and established a *kaidu* ordination platform for him;

though the King bestowed upon him the purple robe, the Master would not accept it. At that time, the poet Zheng Shuo traveled south and personally attended the Master’s noble conduct, composing a poem as a gift for him.
It is said: "The purple robes on the rack remain unworn; the golden characters on the desk are gazed upon for long. The Master lectured on the *Lotus Sūtra* some fifty times.
One day, while he was preaching in the lecture hall, a lotus flower suddenly sprang forth, with double stalks and layered petals, its fragrance rich and pervasive.
To this day, Yongjia is esteemed as a treasure among the Sangha.
Shi Kezhou of Longxing Temple in Hangzhou, Wuyue, was born into the Fu family of Jinling.

Having left the household life, he traveled to Yuzhang, where he thoroughly investigated the *Fahua jing* and the Great Commentary of Ci’en. Subsequently, he went to Longxing Temple to expound the *Lotus Sūtra*, with a constant assembly of several hundred monastics and laypeople.
King Qian Wusuku commissioned the Master to the Tianbao Hall to lecture on the sūtra for the spirits of the underworld at night; this occurred frequently.

He saw various ghosts and spirits manifesting their forms to serve as his attendants and guardians. Once, there was a shaman performing a sacrifice at the shrine of the God of the Bronze Official; after a long time, the deity did not descend.
Later, the spirit spoke through the medium, saying, "I have been attending the Dharma from the Hall of Heavenly Treasure with the Great Deity and am only now returning.

Wukuo was astonished by this and bestowed upon the Master a golden *ruyi* scepter along with an alms bowl, granting him the title Tongming. He also authored one scroll of the *Fahua xu cao* (Commentary on the Preface to the Lotus Sutra).

Shi Zixin of Yingrui Monastery in Xuanzhou during the Jin dynasty washed away his transgressions through the precepts and sought out teachers. He studied the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* with such refinement that he never once grew weary or negligent.
Once, while entering the mountains of Xuancheng to gather medicinal herbs, he penetrated deep into a cave until it became dark. Suddenly, he beheld the light of the sun.
After traveling several li, there was a separate opening by the side of the cave where the mountain stream flowed gently. There, beneath a great pine tree, he saw a grass hut. One...
The monk Xue-mei sat in meditation, wrapped in his robes. Beside him were a small bell and fire-making implements.

When the Master struck the bell, the monk emerged from samādhi. Opening his eyes in surprise, he said, "Ah! By what means have you come here? The Master then recounted his travels. The monk bowed and invited him to sit;

he took a stone to strike for fire and brewed tea, the fragrance and flavor of which were most delightful. At evening, the monk yielded his hut to the Master for the night and looked after the other monk.

Within a large nest atop a pine tree, he heard the sound of the *Lotus Sūtra* being recited; the voice was exceptionally clear and resonant. After a short while, a monk shouted and scolded, saying, "This pack of beasts!
Having now become members of the fur-bearing species, why do you cause living people such distress? Return quickly to the thickets; you should not venture out at will.
The Master peered down and saw a group of tigers and leopards departing with their ears flattened against their necks. When dawn broke, the monk came down from the pine tree to meet him.
The Master requested that the monk attend to his handkerchief and sandals. The monk said, "From here on, one sees nothing but withered grass for hundreds of li;
it is four miles from any human habitation and is no place for you to dwell. He further asked, "Are you not hungry? By the streamside there were over a hundred stalks of rice.

He gathered the grain, scooped three handfuls of rice, picked some wild vegetables, and boiled them together to give to him to eat. He then sent him back, escorting him as far as the mouth of the cave and saying, "Our meeting was no mere coincidence."
This was indeed so. Regarding the tea and vegetable gruel he consumed, his lifelong diet was never lacking. The Master then followed the path back to his own monastery.
More than a month had passed, and he ordered his companions to go search for him once more; however, the location of the cave could not be found.
These events took place during the Tianfu era of Emperor Wenmu of Wuyue.
Shi Yichu of Kaiyuan Temple in Qizhou during the Zhou dynasty was born into the Pei clan of Xiangzhou.

At the age of seven, he left the household life and took refuge in the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*, prostrating himself before every single character until he had completed the entire text. He reached the subtlest depths and attained the ultimate mastery of the *Abhidharmakośa* school.

He compiled the *Six Categories of Buddhist Notes* (*Shishi liutie*), beginning from the "Appearance of the Dharma King" section and ending with the "Lion and Animal Species" section; it became a magnificent and voluminous work that brought great renown.

In the first year of the Dede era, an imperial edict ordered that [the master’s works] be submitted to the Historiographic Office. Initially, when the Master was composing his *Zuan*, he lost the sight of both eyes;

no medical practitioner could cure him. Thereupon, he settled his mind in repentance for his transgressions. Thus, with such unceasing devotion, his vision was restored after two years. People regarded this as a sign of spiritual resonance.
Shi Shaoyan of the Song dynasty was of the Liu clan from Yongzhou. He had perused and thoroughly mastered all the various scriptures.
Upon entering the Wu and Kuaiji regions, he hung up his monk’s staff at Suixin Temple in Hangzhou. There, he constantly recited the *Lotus Sūtra* without ceasing day or night.

Suddenly, lotus flowers sprang up upon the dry land, drawing the gaze of the entire city. In the second year of the Jianlong era, when his vow for the recitation was fulfilled, he vowed to emulate the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja.

He prepared to cremate his body. At that time, Qian, the King of Hannan, earnestly entreated him to stay, and he finally desisted. Shortly thereafter, he again sought to throw himself into the Cao-e River to feed the fish’s bellies;
however, as if supported by a divine being, his feet were held up, and amidst the surging, violent waves, it was as if he were sitting upon a jeweled terrace.
The King then constructed Shangfang Monastery and invited the Master to reside there. In the fourth year of the Kaibao era, he spoke to his attendants: "I have recited the Lotus Sutra, and..."

He recited twenty thousand sections [of scripture] and was determined to take rebirth in the Land of Peaceful Nurturing (An-yang) as his goal. Now, having fortunately fulfilled this aspiration, he spoke these words and then sat in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*) and passed away.
His cremation yielded countless relics (*śarīra*), and the remaining bones were as translucent and lustrous as jade.
Shi Xi-ji of the Song dynasty was of the Hu family in Yongjia. In his childhood, he recited the *Lotus Sūtra* and mastered it within a month.
After receiving full ordination, he visited Master Song of Mount Tiantai to study and investigate the *Śamatha-vipaśyanā*.

He once stayed at Yuwang Temple in Siming and dreamed that he ascended to the upper story of Guoqing Temple, where there was a jeweled dais inscribed with the words "Mañjuśrī’s Platform. It was enclosed by a railing, and though he wished to enter, he could not.
"Very well. Shortly thereafter, he saw Guanyin emerge from within the temple, lingering to meet him. From then on, his joyful exposition of the Dharma was inexhaustible.
He subsequently gave successive lectures and instructions at Fulong and Guoqing, and when he established the Luoxi Doctrinal Center, his disciples gathered like clouds.
In the fifth year of the Taiping Xingguo era, he traveled to Huangyan to release living beings into the Yangtze River and lectured on the "Chapter of the Elder Stream-Water" until he reached Haimen.

At Lingshi, Zhizhe re-established his winter retreat at the Daochang Monastery, which subsequently flourished as a renowned monastery. Throughout his life, he lectured on the *Lotus Sūtra* more than ten times.
As the local customs of the Ou and Yue regions were formerly devoted to hunting, after hearing the Master’s instructions, everyone cast away their bows and tore their nets;
such was the unprecedented success of his preaching.
The Song dynasty monk Yitong, surnamed Yin, was of Korean descent. His physical features were extraordinary; his eyebrows measured more than five inches in length.

He left home at a young age at Guishanyuan Monastery. During the Tianfu era of the Jin dynasty, he traveled to the Central Land and arrived at the abode of National Teacher Yunju Shao of Tiantai, where he suddenly attained awakening.
Upon visiting Luoxi, he heard the principle of the "three contemplations in one mind" and sighed, saying:

"The study of the Perfect and Sudden [Teachings] has reached its ultimate goal here. Consequently, he remained to receive instruction. After some time, he wished to board a ship and return eastward to his own country.

Qian Weizhi, the Governor of Siming, earnestly entreated him to stay, saying, "If you merely intend to benefit sentient beings, why must you go to Koryo? The Master then stayed at Chuanjiao Monastery.
In the sixth year of the Taiping Xingguo era, it was granted the name Baoyun Monastery. There, the Master extensively propagated the teachings and contemplations.
After some twenty years, in the first year of the Duan-gong era, he passed away while reclining on his right side.
The Song dynasty monk Wuen was the son of the Lu family of Luyou. During the Changxing era, he went to Huiju Temple in Kunshan to study the Nanshan Vinaya.

Later, hearing of the Three Contemplations of Tiantai, he found a profound resonance between them and his own latent understanding; he subsequently traveled to Ziguang Monastery in Qiantang to seek instruction from Master Zhi.
Under his teacher, he studied for many years; he thoroughly penetrated the profound subtleties of the *Fahua guangming zhiguan lun*.

In the eighth month of the third year of the Yongxi era, he dreamed of a shaven-headed monk clad in *kāṣāya* robes, holding a golden incense burner and burning incense, who circumambulated his room three times, declaring himself to be the Patriarch Guanding coming to welcome him.
Upon waking from the dream, he still smelled a wondrous fragrance; facing west with palms joined, he passed away at the monastery.
Within [the mountain], they all heard the sounds of stringed instruments, flutes, bells, and chimes from the void; these sounds seemed to drift vaguely toward the west.
Shi Xingnian of Shoushan in Ruzhou, Song, was born into the Di clan of Lai Prefecture. He received his training at Nan Chan Temple in his native prefecture.
He traveled extensively among various monastic assemblies and constantly recited the *Lotus Sūtra* in secret; thus, the community called him "The One Who Recites the Lotus.
Later, he attended upon Fengxue. One day, while the Master and Zhen, the head gardener, were together paying their respects, Fengxue asked, "What is that which the World-Honored One does not speak?
Zhen replied, "A magpie on the treetop. Fengxue said, "Why do you perform such foolish merit? What..."
He did not investigate the meaning of the words and phrases. He again questioned the Master, who said: "Moving one's countenance reveals the ancient path;
do not fall into the trap of silent stillness. Xue said to Zhen: "Why do you not look at the sub-commentary on the *Lotus Sūtra*?

On the fourth day of the twelfth month of the third year of the Chunhua era, he ascended the hall and spoke a verse containing the words: "This year’s record shall serve as next year’s event. On the [specific] day of the fourth year, [he passed away].
Not deviating from what was previously recorded, he ascended the hall and spoke this verse: "All you disciples wander aimlessly; how many Ganges Rivers have you already crossed?
Guanyin points to Maitreya; even Manjusri can do nothing about it. After a long while, he passed away peacefully. His body was cremated, and five-colored śarīra relics were obtained.
The Song dynasty monk Zhili, styled Fazhi, was surnamed Jin and was a native of Siming. He received the Tiantai teachings and contemplations from Master Tong Baoyun.

During the Chunhua era, his spiritual influence flourished greatly, and students gathered like a forest. He diligently practiced the *Lotus Sūtra* and the *Pratyutpanna Samādhi*, vowing to be reborn in the Land of Peaceful Nurturing (*An-yang*).
He once gathered ten like-minded companions to perform the repentance rites; when the three-year period was complete, he intended to practice self-immolation.

Regarding the *Bao Miao Jing* (The Sutra of the Wondrous Retribution), Yang Wen Gong Yi and Li Gong Zunxu petitioned for the Master to be granted the rank of Zifu and the title of Dharma-Wisdom Great Master (*Fazhi Dashi*).
By imperial decree, he was requested to remain in the world. His disciple Benru requested instruction on the intent of the King of Sutras.

The Master said, "Serve as my head of the monastery (*jianyuan*) for three years. Benru followed these instructions. When the three years had concluded, he again consulted the Master. The Master manifested a majestic and awe-inspiring presence.
"Hè! With a sudden clarity, he presented this verse: "Everywhere I meet the path home; At every moment, I am in my native land.
This is the reality already manifest from the beginning— Why must one wait for deliberation? His spontaneous awakening was like this. For the rest of his life, the Master practiced repentance.
When the twenty-one-day period was completed, he recited [the name] seven times. Master Zhizhe of the Tiantai school served as the standard;

he authored the *Miaozongchao*, which greatly elucidated the principles of contemplating the mind and contemplating the Buddha. On the New Year’s Day of the sixth year of the Tiānshèng era, he established the *Guānmíng Chàn* (Practise of Light).

By the fifth day, he summoned the assembly to preach the Dharma, suddenly chanting the Buddha’s name several hundred times before sitting in the full lotus posture and passing away. His remains were left in the open for two weeks, yet his countenance remained unchanged.

His physical features remained as they were at birth; his fingernails and hair grew long together, and his tongue remained unimpaired like a lotus flower. Zhao Qingxian Gong Bian composed an inscription for his stupa.

The lineage was transmitted from Nāgārjuna to Wen of the Northern Qi, Wen to Sengsi of Mount Nanyue, Sengsi to Zhiyi of Tiantai, and continuing down to Fazhi, who became the seventeenth patriarch of the Tiantai school.

Shi Zunshe, style name Zhibai, was a native of the Ye family of Ninghai. He entered Guoqing Temple and, before the image of Samantabhadra, burned off one of his fingers, vowing to transmit the teachings and contemplations of Tiantai.
At the beginning of the Yongxi era, he visited Master Tong Baoyun; his wisdom and understanding were exceptionally outstanding.
On the anniversary of the death of the Great Master Zhiyi, he burned his crown and vowed to practice the four samādhis with diligent effort. He subsequently returned to Tiantai.

Through arduous study, he vomited blood; yet he resolutely pursued the Way for a full seven weeks. Suddenly, as if in a dream, he saw Avalokiteśvara extending his hand into his mouth and drawing out several worms.
The Master then further extended his fingers and poured nectar into his mouth; his body and mind became cool and refreshed, and his chronic illness was instantly cured.
In the eighth year of the Xiangfu era, he moved his residence to Tiantzhu. During the Tianxi era, the Duke Wenmu Wang governed Hangzhou.
He first visited Master [Zhili] at Mount Shishan and requested that he lecture on the *Lotus Sūtra* and the principle of the three dharmas—mind, Buddha, and sentient beings—as being identical.

Zhiyi’s eloquence was clear and inspired; the Duke sighed in admiration and ceased not to praise him. He requested the bestowal of the name "Compassionate Cloud" (*Ciyun*) and established the Riguān Hermitage to the east of the temple as a place for the practice of visualizing the Western Pure Land.
Based on the *Sūtra of Immeasurable Life*, he composed the *Ritual for Repentance for Rebirth in the Pure Land* and practiced it accordingly.
The *Yuàn* (Vow) Dharma-gate flourished widely in the world. He constantly practiced the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-samādhi* for a period of ninety days, and his spiritual responses were manifold.
He constructed a Hall of Light for Repentance; for every rafter he set up and every brick he laid, he would invariably recite the *Mahākaruṇā-dhāraṇī* seven times.

Although it was repeatedly ravaged by war and fire, it remained standing alone and majestic, due to the power of his vows. In the tenth year of the Tiānshèng era, he manifested his passing. At that time...
He was titled the Chan Master Ciyun.
The Dharma Master Fazhiyan of Kai bao Temple in the Song dynasty, a Mahāsattva of the Lotus Sūtra, claimed himself to be of the Xu clan from Shouchun.

In his early twenties, he traveled to the Eastern Capital (Luoyang) and received ordination at Qijuzhi Monastery. One day, while reading the records of Yunmen, he suddenly attained awakening. Not long after, his former...

His life’s mission was thus fulfilled. His physical features were extraordinary and ancient; he gazed straight ahead without blinking, and his speech flowed on incessantly, its meaning beyond comprehension.
He never ceased his daily recitations and, as he constantly delighted in chanting the *Lotus Sūtra*, he took that as his title. At the time of his passing, he said to others:
"Since immeasurable kalpas past, I have accomplished the land of Jetavana and manifested my body to propagate the teachings. Now I am returning south. Thereupon, he passed away.

He passed away with a serene countenance. Emperor Renzong once burned incense and prayed silently at night, saying, "Tomorrow, I shall invite the Great Being of the Lotus Sūtra (Fahua Dashishi) to a vegetarian feast in the Huicheng Hall.
At dawn, an inner attendant reported that Fahua had come directly from the Right Yek Gate, proceeding straight toward the Imperial Palace;
though they tried to stop him, he could not be turned back. The Emperor smiled and said, "I invited him to come. When he arrived, he went straight up to the imperial throne.
He sat cross-legged upon his mat and accepted the offerings. When the Emperor asked about the succession to the throne, he took up his brush and wrote large characters: "Thirteen, thirteen.
Later, when Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, he was indeed the thirteenth son of Prince An-yi of Pu.

When Lü Wenmu Mengzheng requested to speak on the *Lotus Sūtra* ritual and asked about future fortunes and misfortunes, he merely took up his brush and wrote the two characters "Bozhou. This was when he had resigned from the position of Chancellor.
He served as the Prefect of Bozhou. It was then that he first realized the meaning of the previous prophecy.
Shi Benru of Nengren Temple on Mount Dongye in Song was a native of Jiu Zhang in Siming.

Having followed the teachings of Fazhi since childhood, in the fourth year of the Xiangfu era, he went to the Eastern Mountain (Dongshan), where he extensively propagated the teachings of the Contemplation and the Contemplation of the Infinite Life Sutra, as well as preaching the Lotus Sutra and the *Prabhāsa-sūtra*.
He recited the sutras six or seven times each day. Furthermore, he assembled one hundred monks and performed the long repentance ritual of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* for one year.
Once, while at the southwest of the mountain, he saw a tiger lying down; striking it with his staff, he said, "This is not your dwelling place. The tiger lowered its head and departed.

Later, he built a hermitage at the spot where the tiger had lain and retired within it. Previously, a deity possessing the five supernatural powers had resided there; whenever the Master sat in meditation, the deity would appear.

While sitting, he would frequently be carried through the air on a couch joined with others. Admiring the style of Mount Lu, he formed the White Lotus Society together with the worthy men Xun Gong and Zhang Dexiang.
During the Qingli era, an imperial edict conferred upon him the title Shenzhao and a purple square robe; the temple was granted the name Bailian.
Later, as he preached the Dharma and prepared for his departure, those on the river saw a monk ascending into the clouds and heading west.
In the fourth year of the Jiading era, he was reinterred. Although two hundred years had already passed, upon opening the casket, his compassionate countenance remained solemn;
his beard and hair hung long, and śarīras filled the reliquary chamber.
Shi Zushao of Lingyin and Tianzhu Monasteries in the Song dynasty was of the Liu clan of Tiantai. At the age of nineteen, he had mastered the recitation of the *Lotus Sūtra*.

He entered the Eastern掖 (掖) [the capital] to study under Ciyun, from whom he fully grasped the profound essentials. He devoted himself solely to the practice of the *Lotus Samādhi*, making it his regular daily discipline.

Once, while performing the *Guangming Repentance* for one hundred days and nights, when the period was nearly half over, he suddenly saw banners and streamers filling the space before him, and a guide called out to him.
He became the Great Discerning Honored Deity (Mahāmaṃjuśrī). The Master immediately stepped forward and bowed; the deity said, "Your Reverence transmits the Mahāyāna, bringing vast benefit to many.
Having spoken, he vanished. Furthermore, while traveling along the Huai and Si rivers, the Master dreamed of a monk who placed his hand upon his head and said, "I am the Upādhyāya Mañjuśrī."
I shall show you the five meanings of non-arising. Once awakened, the five treasuries [of his mind] opened wide, like chewing ice and snow.
Shi Youyan, a monk of the Song dynasty, was of Hu origin from Linhai. At age fourteen, he went to Dongshan to rely upon Shenzhao, where he studied the teachings and contemplations of Tiantai.
During the Shaosheng era, he lived in seclusion on the eastern peak of Chicheng, binding a thatched hut beneath a jujube tree; consequently, he styled himself:
Chaa-an practiced the Lotus Samādhi. Whenever there were prayers for relief from drought or floods, he would perform recitations; his miraculous responses were like echoes following sounds.
His mother suffered from eye disease, so the Master, facing the Great Being Avalokiteśvara, visualized the *sūryakānta-maṇi* (sun-crystal) in the Bodhisattva’s hand.

The mother then dreamed that the Master held the sun before her; upon waking, her eyes were restored to clarity. One day, while in meditative concentration, she saw a celestial deity tell her, "The Master has perfected his pure karma."

Furthermore, he dreamed that a great lotus flower grew from the midst of a pond, with celestial music arranged in four rows; he then composed a piece titled "A Farewell to the West" to show to the assembly.
Seven days later, he passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture. Above his stupa there was a light like the moon, which did not vanish until three o'clock in the afternoon.

Shi Chuxian of the Song dynasty was from the Wang clan of Tiantai. After receiving full ordination, he reflected that the Buddha-dharma is vast and profound; if one does not study it with diligence, how can one realize the Way?
He immediately entered Tianfeng Monastery to read the Tripitaka, completing it in three years. He then went to visit Shenzhao, through whom he gained a deep understanding of the doctrinal principles.
Later, he presided over Bailian Monastery and transmitted the teachings and contemplations of the Tiantai school. He constantly practiced the Lotus Samādhi. Yuan...
In the seventh month of the first year of the Yuanshou era, he summoned the assembly and distributed his robes and alms bowl, saying: "On the twenty-third day, I shall return to the Pure Land.
Instruct the attendants that when the morning bell rings, they should inform me. When the time arrived, he rose slowly, sat in the full lotus posture, and passed away.
Yang Cigong composed a eulogy for him, which says: "The letter was sealed and he sat in the full lotus; not dwelling in the white lotus, he gave birth to a white lotus."

Shi Lingzhao of the Song dynasty was of the Lu clan of Dongyang. From birth, she vowed her resolve for the gates of emptiness. Before a month had passed, she had mastered the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* and the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra*.
Carrying her book-box to the school, she refined her studies of the Three Contemplations of Tiantai. Later, she resided at Chaoguo Temple in Huating.
During the Yuanfeng era, she gathered various virtuous companions to establish a Pure Society (*jing-she*) to emulate the tradition of Donglin. She once saw [him] in a dream.
The Master knelt and asked the Three Sages of Amitābha whether his lifelong recitation of sutras and prayers for rebirth in the Pure Land had been fulfilled.
Avalokiteśvara pointed and said, "The Pure Land is not far; if you have the vow, you shall be born there. Do not doubt it further.

Furthermore, while reciting sutras on a quiet night, he beheld Samantabhadra in a dream. Consequently, he resolved to create images of Bodhisattvas and vowed to recite ten thousand copies of the Lotus Sutra.
Yan Jingbao, while in meditative concentration one day, beheld extraordinary signs. He then sat with his feet crossed and passed away.
Upon cremation, his tongue remained unburnt, and countless śarīras were produced.
The Song dynasty monk Shi Kejiu resided at Kaiyuan Temple in Siming. He constantly recited the Lotus Sūtra and was thus known as "Jiu Fahua" (Lotus-Dharma Longevity).

The Master was on the most intimate terms with Su Wenzhong Gong (Su Shi). While staying at Xiangfu Temple on West Lake, his single room was desolate; he maintained a life of purity and integrity, adhering to poverty.
Once, during the lantern festival at Jiuqu, when the official had departed with his attendants, he walked alone into the Master’s quarters, where there was not a single lamp.
When the fire was lit, only the lingering fragrance of *campaka* flowers could be smelled. The Duke sighed in admiration and left behind a poem containing the lines:

"Only when one does not use lapis lazuli to idly illuminate the Buddha does one first know that the inexhaustible is fundamentally not a lamp. In the eighth year of the Yuanyou era, he passed away while sitting upright without illness.

After three days, he revived and said, "I have already traveled in spirit to the Pure Land and beheld its features; they accord with those described in the *Sutra of the Sixteen Contemplations*. Its magnificence... [text ends].
The inscriptions were identical. Within the ponds of the seven treasures, all the lotus pedestals bore the names of those destined to be reborn there.
On one pedestal of purple-gold was written: "Master Xun of Guangjiao Monastery, Chengdu Prefecture"—he has already been reborn therein.
On another golden pedestal was written: "Mr. Sun, the twelfth son, of Mingzhou. On another was written: "Kejiu. On yet another silver pedestal was written: "Madame Xu, of Mingzhou."
Having finished speaking, he vanished again through transformation. Five years later, Xu Dao died as usual; a strange fragrance filled the room. Seven years after that, Sun Shierlang passed away;
at that time, the sound of celestial music was heard welcoming him into the void. All these events occurred exactly as the Master had foretold.
Shi Jizhong of Faming Monastery in Wenzhou, Song, was born into the Qiu family of Yongjia. He received the full precepts at the age of eight and went to Nanhu to rely upon Guangzhi.
He attained profound insight into the teachings and contemplations (*jiaoguan*) and practiced the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* and *Prabhāsa* Samādhis without a single day of idleness.

He cured illnesses and exorcised malevolent spirits with unfathomable spiritual efficacy. In the fifth year of the Yuanfeng era, he gathered the assembly to preach the Dharma and passed away amidst a brilliant red light that illuminated everything.
In the void, the entire assembly of the Pure Society perceived a vision. A deity clad in golden armor appeared in a dream and announced: "Dharma Master Zhong has already been reborn in Tuṣita.
Shi Sizhao of the Yang clan from Yangtong, a monk of the Song dynasty, attained a profound resonance with the divine through his contemplation.

Thereafter, he drew blood to transcribe seven fascicles of the *Lotus Sūtra* and constructed a small hermitage called Deyun. He devoted himself exclusively to the practice of the Buddha-remembrance samādhi for thirty years during the Xuanhe era.
In the first year of his era, during the spring, one night he beheld the Buddha manifesting in a golden body. He immediately formed a mudrā and sat in transformation.

The Master recited the Lotus Sūtra one thousand times; for each word of the seven Pure Land sūtras, he performed a prostration. Furthermore, he prostrated himself ten times over the Lotus Sūtra. His ascetic practices were beyond compare.
Shi Zhongli of Mingzhou, Song, was born into the Chen family of Yin. He entered the monastic order at the age of seven and was granted the title Mingzhi.
During the Xining era, he resided at Nanhu and succeeded Shenzhi on the abbatial seat, daily expounding *śamatha-vipaśyanā*. In the Yuanyou era, he once again presided over Yanqing Temple.
The Master practiced the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-samādhi-bhāvanā-vidhi* for seven years. As his practice was nearing completion, one day during meditative contemplation he saw a great boat;

though the multitude wished to board it, they could not, and only the Master sat within it as he proceeded. From that time on, his discernment and wisdom gushed forth like a spring. He recited the *Lotus Sūtra* more than ten thousand times.
In performing rites to avert calamities and alleviate droughts, there was nothing that did not manifest divine efficacy. Thus, he supported the school in Yongjia.
He said to his master, "I once saw the Great Mārīcī-Vajrapāṇi seeking to protect the Dharma within a dream.

On another day, I hope you will kindly provide a place for him in the hall of repentance. When the master presided over the rite of repentance, it was he who first established the image. Chen Yingzhong once praised the master, saying:
"He strictly purified the *vinaya* and firmly maintained pure contemplation; using his body as a tongue, he expounded upon ten billion matters."
Shi Jingfan of the Zhuzhi family from Jiahe was a monk at Wuliangshou Yuan in Gusu during the Song dynasty.
At the beginning of the Yuanyou era, he presided over Daci Monastery in Gusu and lectured on the *Lotus Sūtra* more than ten times.

During the Daguan era, he gathered twenty-seven monks to perform the *Lotus Repentance*, establishing a ritual period of twenty-eight days for each session. After three such assemblies, he was moved by the manifestation of Samantabhadra.
During the *karmavācanā* for receiving the precepts, when the name of the pure *brahmacārin* monk was called out, his deep voice resounded like the striking of a great bell.
As his *samādhi* was about to reach completion, two monks prostrated themselves and said, "This spring we came to Shiqiao to pay homage to the sacred traces;

suddenly we saw flowers scattering from the sky, and an extraordinary fragrance unlike any other. One monk remarked in haste, "The Dharma Master Fan of Gusu has invited us to the repentance ceremony where flowers will scatter."

Having spoken thus, he vanished from sight. Consequently, [the Master] came to pay his respects. Later, while at a repentance assembly, he saw the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa patrolling the confession hall.
Whenever a practitioner was being scrutinized, the King would suddenly shield them and withdraw. During the Yuánfú era, the Master once dreamed that he had arrived at the underworld.
There, the King welcomed him to take his seat and ordered an official to consult the registers, saying: "The Bhikṣu Jingfàn has frequently undergone many..."
Jie. He lectured on the Lotus Sūtra for a long time. The King immediately rose, prostrated himself, and dispatched an envoy to escort him back.
At the end of the Zhenghe era, after he manifested his passing, there were five-colored śarīra relics.
Shi Tan Yi of the Song dynasty was of the Du clan from Yaocheng. He left home to become a monk at Longquan Temple in his youth and had already studied the teachings and contemplations of Tiantai.

He sealed himself within a retreat to specialize in the practice of Pure Land Buddhism. He recited the *Lotus Sūtra* five thousand times and the *Universal Worthy Contemplation Sūtra* and the *Amitābha Sūtra* ten thousand scrolls each.

He maintained the chanting of the Buddha’s name without interruption every day. At the beginning of the Chongning era, he burned incense and addressed the assembly, saying: "I shall be reborn in the Pure Land..."
"The time has come for me to depart this world. You shall mount the vajra-throne and follow the Buddha as he journeys westward. I pray that you exert yourself in cultivation;
then you may meet me. Having spoken these words, he passed away peacefully.
Shi Zongli of the Gao family from Gaoyi in Kuaiji of the Song dynasty had received full ordination.
He went to Gusu to rely upon Shenwu, where he practiced the Lotus Repentance for a period of three years, at the end of which he suddenly saw Samantabhadra passing before him through the air.

Subsequently, he traveled to Bishuo in Xincheng to specialize in the practice of the Buddha-remembrance samādhi (*nienfo sanmei*). In the first year of the Zhenghe era, during a drought, he prayed for rain and moved the dragon.
The King manifested his golden-hued body, and sweet rain fell in abundance. At the end of the Jianyan era, he resided at Mount Daowei, fixing his mind on the Pure Land.
On the third night, the pearl atop the head of a painted image suddenly emitted a brilliant light. One day, he told his disciples, "The Buddha is coming;
I shall return to An-yang. He then wrote a verse: "The man of the Way with a single mark returns home; The golden terrace awaits."
He sat and cut off the narrowness of heaven and earth with his verse; then, he passed away suddenly.
Śramaṇa Daochin of Wenzhou in the Song dynasty was born into the Peng family of Leqing. At eighteen, he received the full precepts and went to Nanhu to rely upon Yuanzhao.
While in meditative concentration, he beheld the Venerable Master Siming seated upon his meditation couch, engaging in a profound discourse on the characteristics of dharmas (*dharmalakṣaṇa*).

From that time forth, his mind was suddenly enlightened. Consequently, while practicing the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-samādhi*, he was moved by the Great Being Samantabhadra emitting light, whereby his wisdom and eloquence increased all the more.
There was a man suffering from a chronic illness; for him, [the Master] preached the Dharma and offered food, whereby he recovered his health and peace.

Toward the end of the Shaoxing era, he suddenly gathered the assembly to chant the *Amitābha Sūtra* (Guānjīng) day and night without ceasing. The assembly smelled a wondrous fragrance that filled the hall. The Master said, "The Buddha has come to welcome me.

He then bathed and changed his robes, and while the assembly had not yet finished chanting the "Chapter on Peaceful Conduct" (*Anle xing pin*), he sat peacefully and passed away. His shrine remained for over a month.
Yan’s [statue] appears as if alive.
The Song dynasty monk Congya was a native of Qiantang. Initially, he followed Haiyue and mastered the study of *śamatha* and *vipaśyanā*.

He subsequently entered the Tianwang Temple on Mount Nan-shan, where he recited the *Lotus Sūtra* more than twenty thousand times. He also recited various other sūtras and performed prostrations to the Buddha until he had completed one million bows.
He venerated the *Lotus Sūtra* by performing three prostrations for each single character. With his heart set upon the Pure Land, he sat throughout his life never turning away from the west.
Such was his sincerity that the Imperial Commissioner Yang Jie composed thirty hymns in praise of the Land of Peace and Bliss to present to the Master.
One of his verses says: "The Pure Land pervades the entire Dharma-realm; why labor to point only toward the West? If one can enter through any single gate, every place is Bodhi.
The Master depicted the nine grades of samādhi at Jingzhu Temple and carved praises upon stone. Many people were moved and transformed by him.

Later, he passed away while sitting upright without illness, accompanied by the scent of extraordinary incense and the sound of celestial music. All considered this a sign that the Western Sage had come to welcome him.
The Song dynasty monk Shi Hanyi received the teachings and contemplations of the Tiantai school. He once transcribed the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* using silver ink;

whenever he encountered the names of Buddhas or Bodhisattvas, he used gold ink. The world regarded this as a supreme treasure of the Dharma. During the Jianyan era, when the Jin invaders arrived, the temple buildings were burned to the ground.
Amidst the rubble, this scripture was recovered, not a single character damaged.

The Song dynasty monk Shi Zunan resided at Yunfeng Peak on Mount Nanyue. He drew blood to transcribe five hundred fascicles of the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra*, one hundred fascicles of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāra-mitā Sūtra*, and ten sets of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*.
Over the course of twenty-seven years, he used his own blood for all of these writings.

In his final years, his blood dried up and he stood as mere skin and bone; yet the sound of him reciting the Buddha’s name never ceased. One day, while sitting in the abbot’s quarters, he passed away amidst the transformation of his body.
From between his eyebrows, śarīras burst forth, appearing one after another as soon as they were taken.
Yu Sijing of Song was a native of Qiantang. He styled himself the "Son of the Pure Land. In his youth, he attended Master Ying’s lectures on the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*.

Later, he constantly recited the sutra and devoted himself single-mindedly to the practice of Buddha-recollection (*nienfo*). In his leisure time, he would paint images of the Buddha. Whenever he painted, he would first enter a pure chamber and meditate in stillness until he beheld the radiance of Amitābha;
only then would he take up his brush. In the year Dingyi of the Shaoxing era, he sat upright for seven days with one-pointed mind.
He recited the Buddha’s name and passed away peacefully.
Zuo Shen, a retired scholar of the Song dynasty from Linhai in Tiantai, received the Bodhisattva precepts from Shenzhao.

He carved images of the Three Sages of the Western Paradise and served them with devotion day and night. He recited the Lotus Sūtra three thousand four hundred times and the Diamond Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra [three thousand four hundred times].
In the autumn of the second year of the Shaosheng era, he ordered the śramaṇa Chang to recite the opening title of the *Lotus Sūtra* and received the Bodhisattva precepts in addition.
Shortly thereafter, he dreamed of three eminent figures standing on the riverbank, who summoned him to board a boat; he immediately requested a monk to recite the *Amitābha Sūtra*.
He suddenly said, "I have already seen the Buddha's light," and sat upright until he passed away.
Fan Yan of Renhe, Song dynasty, regularly subsisted on vegetarian food and was detached from worldly affairs, saying, "I am merely a traveler passing through."
He recited the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* daily and personally transcribed a copy of the scripture with the utmost magnificence.

During the Daguang era, he suddenly beheld Samantabhadra riding a six-tusked white elephant and emitting golden light. The Bodhisattva addressed Zhiyan, saying, "Because you have constantly recited the *Lotus Sutra* and kept Amitābha Buddha in mind, you shall attain birth in the Pure Land;
therefore, I have come to inform you. One night later, he saw a multitude of holy beings extending their hands to him as he approached.
He sat with palms joined and passed away.

During the Xiangfu era of the Song dynasty, Zhang Qing of Bianjing served as a jailer. He always maintained himself with compassion and caution, personally attending to the cleaning and sweeping every day, being especially diligent during the hot months.
Regarding food, drink, medicine, and bedding, he invariably ensured they were refined and pure. He frequently exhorted his subordinates:
He said, "When people are unfortunately caught by the law, if we of our kind do not know how to show them compassion, then where will the offenders go to lodge their grievances?

Throughout my life, I have maintained the recitation of the Lotus Sutra; whenever I encounter a heavy prisoner being led to execution, I invariably observe a vegetarian fast and recite the sutra for them."

He ceased [his practice] after one month. He once instructed a prisoner in jail, saying: "If you have committed a crime, you should confess it yourself; do not falsely incriminate the innocent to increase your own karmic retribution.
His wife, Lady Yuan, died of an epidemic at the age of forty-eight. After three days, she suddenly revived and said:
"When I first arrived, I was in a foul place and longed for a cool, refreshing spot. Suddenly, I saw the Great Being in white robes who said to me: 'You ought not to be here.'"
Furthermore, she had not yet borne any offspring. "Your husband has accumulated much hidden virtue; among his descendants, there shall surely be those who flourish," he said.

He then took her by the hand and led her outside, where she regained consciousness. The following year, she gave birth to a son, Heng, who was appointed as a Third Class Borrowed Official (*sānbān jièzhí*). She lived to the age of eighty-two and passed away without illness.
Her six grandsons all held prominent offices, and their family came to be known as a distinguished clan.

Li Yu, the Commissioner of the Wubei Army in the Song dynasty, was a habitual reciter of the *Lotus Sūtra*. One night, while traveling on a dark road, he encountered a pack of ghosts who insulted him.
Suddenly, an old man appeared, wearing a coarse robe and straw sandals, who rebuked them with a stern voice, saying, "This man constantly recites the *Lotus Sūtra*;
you must not offend him. Thereupon, the ghosts dispersed, and the old man vanished as well.
Lu Yuan of the Ministry of Justice in the Song Dynasty, styled Sheng’an, lived at Hengxi in Siming.
Every morning upon rising, he would wash his face and enter his pure chamber. There he would burn incense and sit in meditation, reciting the Lotus Sūtra without letting his eyes wander.
He began with this verse: "Washing my hands at dawn, the palm-leaf sutra opens; I seek no blessings, nor do I ward off calamity. Where worldly ties are severed," [he continued].
He severed [all attachments]. Amidst the flames of the kalpa-fire, he performed a single dance; then, opening his scroll, he recited it with a voice like a string of pearls.

He recited it once daily for thirty years. Upon reaching the age of eighty, he increased this to three sections. He composed poetry to express his intent, including the line: "Three times at dawn, I arrive at Mount Ling.
In total, he recited nine thousand four hundred and eighty-five sections. Furthermore, he read the *Vibhāṣā*...
Lu Dazang had extensively researched all the Vinaya sections of the Tiantai school as well as the Mind School of Shaoshi.

Furthermore, he recited the sacred name of Amitābha with single-minded devotion, his thoughts constantly directed toward the West. In the fourth month of the fifth year of the Xiangsho era, at the age of eighty-five, he bathed, donned his ceremonial robes and cap, and passed away.
Suddenly, a fragrance of lotus flowers was perceived emanating from his mouth and nostrils; it remained pervasive for an entire day before finally subsiding.

Chao Shizhi, styled Yidao, was an Imperial Commissioner of the Song dynasty. He once traveled to Hunan to visit Mingzhi and heard his teachings on the "Three Thousand Worlds and Ten Thousand Phenomena.
Delighted, he vowed to study them. In his later years, he recited the Lotus Sūtra daily without ceasing, styling himself the "Old Man of the Lotus Sūtra from the Weishui River."
Zhang Bing of the Song dynasty served as the Prefect of Jizhou. A great bandit plundered the people’s wealth and violated their daughters. Bing was filled with extreme indignation;

he set up a rack, nailed the bandit to it at his gate, and minced him into *hai* (minced meat) over the course of three days. Later, he contracted a feverish ailment (*shai-jing*). One day, just at noon, the illness flared up violently.

Suddenly, he saw an imperial messenger arrive to summon him. He pushed through his illness to urge his horse forward until he reached a palace chamber, where he heard the voice of the late Emperor Zhenzong speaking sternly.
A voice from behind the curtain said, "How can Zhang Bing kill people through unlawful means? Come and debate this with the person himself.
He was led to the southwest corner of the hall, where the prison doors were opened to reveal prisoners in all manner of conditions. He then realized that this was no place of the human world.
One iron-bound criminal had his flesh and blood dripping; weeping, he lamented, "You killed me through unlawful means, and now my limbs are scattered and I shall suffer forever."

"There is no one to take responsibility for this. What can be done? Liang Bing himself admitted that Ji was a thief and reviled him, saying: 'The crime you have committed is more than just a single death;
even if I were to grind ten thousand bodies to dust, it would not suffice to atone for your shame. How dare you appeal further?

Standing nearby was a clerk who had been an old subordinate of Liang Bing during his tenure in Heyang. He said: 'The five punishments have their own established statutes; furthermore, you may not harbor resentment because he appeals.'"
Bing said, "What shall I do? The official said, "Simply send him to take rebirth; you may then return. Bing was terrified and inquired about the method for sending him away.

The official said, "There is no better way than the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*; you must simply promise it with utmost sincerity. Bing then promised that upon his return he would summon monks to recite one hundred sections of the sutra.
When the prisoner did not relinquish [his claim], he increased the number to one thousand sections, yet the result remained the same. Bing became even more afraid. The official said, "No."

"They must have been many. However, for recitation, it is best to do so for a long duration. If you invite one monk to recite one fascicle every day and permit this until the end of his life, then they may be sent away.
Bing agreed to his words and granted the request; consequently, he was no longer seen. Three days later, the deity finally returned.
Thereupon, he summoned a monk daily to recite one fascicle, continuing without interruption until his death. This is recorded in the *Xiangshan yalu*.
The scholar Jiang of Suzhou in the Song dynasty died suddenly in his early twenties. The King of the Netherworld rebuked him, saying: "In your previous life you performed good deeds;
in this life you were destined for eighty-two years. You passed the jinshi examination in the year Dingchou and held successive posts among the high officials.

It was not right that you should kill oxen and eat meat, thereby causing your lifespan to be diminished and your merit cut off. Have you not heard of the thunder and rain on the seventh night in Haizhou, when Heaven sent down—"
"Is this the record of the Stone Drums? The record says: 'Among the six domestic animals, all are products of past karma; yet the ox suffers most bitterly.

Look at those who die by hanging—they are all but people who ate oxen. Having finished speaking, an official standing nearby said to him: 'You ought to seek to restore your soul immediately and reform your ways;
otherwise, you shall be judged to enter hell, from which there will be no time of release. Jiang requested directions, and the official replied: 'The Netherworld...'"

"Those who most reverently transcribe, receive, and uphold the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, and the *Daoshang Ganying Pian*—if you resolve your mind to do so, you may escape [retribution].

If you follow these words and beg for a return to life to reform yourself, transcribe the scriptures, and support your parents, the King of the Netherworld will grant your request, and you shall thus attain rebirth.
Thereafter, he filially supported his two parents, observed the precepts against lust and killing, and transcribed the scriptures.

After maintaining his mantra practice, he constantly recounted these matters to exhort others; those who were moved and transformed by him increased day by day. Later, he passed the imperial examinations and served as a Hanlin Academician.

There was a man from Nanhai in the Song dynasty named Pan Mian, who feigned madness and was unpredictable; people called him Pan’ang, for in the local vernacular, "ang" refers to one whose mind is deranged.
Pan’ang frequently expounded upon the verses and hymns of the *Lotus Sūtra* to people in the capital, visiting them with increasing frequency. One—

A certain person said: "Zhang Ang was none other than the Buddha Sūryaprabha. There was Zhao Tang, who initially served as a幕官 (military official). He resigned his post to follow Zhang Ang and fully attained his Way.
Zhang Ang then vanished into seclusion, and Tang likewise passed away while seated in meditation. By cremating his body, several sheng of śarīra were obtained.
Su Wenzhong Gong Shi associated with Tang’s son, Zhao Chang, and received forty-eight grains [of śarīra]. He once composed the 'Eulogy on Master Zhao's Śarīra'."
Record of Benefits.
When Lu Weng, a butcher from south of the city in Huzhou during the Song dynasty, was twenty-three years old, he saw a wandering monk arrive at his gate.
The monk proclaimed aloud, "I am here to teach and transform those with whom I have a karmic affinity. Lu did not understand him. The monk said, "You have slaughtered countless oxen and sheep."
"Why do you not change your occupation? Lu replied, "I have inherited my ancestral calling; it is difficult to abandon it so abruptly.

The monk said, "If you do not change, in future lives you will surely fall into this same category and continue to suffer retribution for your grievances, with no time of escape. I observe that you possess roots of goodness from past lives."
"You should quickly concentrate your mind on receiving and upholding the Lotus Sūtra and the Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra to eliminate evil karma and increase virtuous merit.
Having spoken these words, he suddenly vanished. Lu was thereby awakened; he observed the fasts and vowed never to slaughter living beings.

He painted a scroll depicting Amitābha Buddha with Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, reverently adorned it for offering, and sought out a teacher to practice the recitation of the two sūtras. Before long—

Within five years, he was able to recite [the scriptures] from memory. Every day before the Buddha, he burned incense and recited one volume of the Lotus Sūtra and one scroll of the Diamond Sūtra, while performing repentance and vowing that the sentient beings he had killed would be delivered to the Pure Land as soon as possible.

At the age of eighty-one, when he was about to depart this world, he made arrangements with his relatives and friends throughout the preceding half-month. On the ninth day of the eleventh month, he prepared a vegetarian meal and took his final leave of them.

When the appointed time arrived, they all went together to the meal. Upon its conclusion, he suddenly requested a bath and changed his robes. Sitting upright, he composed a verse and passed away. The verse said:
"For over sixty years I have abstained from the karma of killing; With hands that cast aside the knife and scale, I practiced in secret. This morning, I have found the path to Bodhi."
A lotus flower born from within fire amidst the water.
Zhu Ruyi of the Song dynasty married into the Xue family of Siming at a young age; when she was over twenty years old, she immediately dwelt in pure seclusion.
Clad in the simple robes of a monastic, she dwelt in seclusion beneath the trees. She embroidered seven scrolls of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*, completing them over ten years.

Upon reaching the "Parable of the Phantom City," she attached *śarīra* relics the size of grains of millet to the needle points; she obtained dozens of such grains in succession. For every single phrase and character, she would chant and prostrate three times.
Furthermore, her embroidery of the images of Amitābha and his two holy attendants was exceedingly marvelous. She also recited various Mahāyāna sūtras.

Like one pouring water from a high roof eaves, he once carved illustrations into woodblocks to encourage people to recite the Buddha’s name; the number of those he converted filled two hundred thousand.
In the fourth year of the Shaohui era, he manifested a slight illness. When a physician offered him cinnabar, he said, "My rebirth in the Pure Land is certain;
what use is there for cinnabar? He then passed away peacefully on his right side. Chan Master Tanzhou Tan composed his biography.

Li Shi, the mother of Dong of Dexing County in the Song dynasty, recited the "Universal Gate Chapter" for over thirty years. Later, she entered the underworld and saw Guanyin extending his hand to lead her away;
his radiance was like daylight. Guanyin said, "Your allotted lifespan has already ended, but because you possess roots of goodness, I have come to assist you. She then suddenly revived.
During the Qingli era of the Song dynasty, when Ou-yang Wen-chung Kung Hsiu was serving as the Governor of Ying-chou, there was an official courtesan named Lu Mei.

She was of elegant and beautiful countenance, and her mouth constantly emitted the fragrance of lotus flowers, which wafted throughout the entire assembly. A monk from Szechuan, who was well-versed in the affairs of people’s past lives, said:
"In a previous existence, this woman was once a nun. For thirty years she recited the Lotus Sūtra; at one point—"

It was a mistake that led to this state of affairs. The official asked the courtesan, "Have you ever read the Lotus Sūtra? She replied, "I have lost myself to this life; it is something I have had no leisure for.
The official ordered the scripture to be brought and showed it to her. Upon reading it once, she recited it immediately as if she had practiced it all her life.
When he attempted to test her with another sutra, however, she was unable to do so. Thereupon, the official finally believed that the words regarding the cultivation of seeds were not false.

During the Shaoxing era of the Song dynasty, there was the mother of Zhao from Fenghua who had long practiced the Lotus Sūtra. A female servant, having eavesdropped for a long time, suddenly remembered four lines:
"The fragrance of blue lotuses, the fragrance of white lotuses, the fragrance of flowering trees, and the fragrance of fruit-bearing trees.
From then on, she recited them incessantly. Later, when she passed away, a single blue lotus flower sprouted at her burial site. Recorded by Shi Benkong.
Huangpo of Mount Chao in Song was a laywoman who had long served the Dharma Flower and the Vajra [Sūtra]. She devoted her heart entirely to the recitation of the Buddha’s name.

Suddenly, she contracted dysentery; she drank only water and took no food. A monk from a neighboring hermitage named Shanxiu dreamed that Huangpo came to him and said, "I am about to depart for the Western Paradise.
Two days later, Huangpo faced west, recited the Buddha’s name, and passed away while sitting upright. Those both near and far all saw a crimson cloud covering Huangpo’s cottage.
Aqin Jingjian of Song lived in Songjiang. She grew weary of her female body and lived separately from her husband.

She strictly observed the precepts and fasts, making it her constant practice to recite the *Lotus Sūtra*, the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, the *Prabhāsa Sūtra*, and the *Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* without ceasing through cold or heat.

She prostrated before the Buddha morning and evening and practiced the Amitābha Repentance. After a long time, a radiant light entered her room; she sat facing west in a state of composure and passed away peacefully.
Lady Lu, titled Song Yini, was a native of Qiantang and the wife of Wang Yu, a Court Petitioner. She constantly recited the *Lotus Sūtra* and devoted her heart to the Pure Land.

She performed one session of ritual repentance and chanted the Buddha’s name ten thousand times every day, never ceasing for thirty years. Later, due to a slight illness, she suddenly heard the celestial drums sounding of their own accord.
While others were struck with wonder and amazement, Lady Lu immediately turned toward the west, joined her hands in mudrā, and passed away.
Shi Hongji, whose style name was Tian’an, was a native of Yao in Yuyao and a monk of Pufu Temple in Yuan-Qiantang.

He lost his father at an early age and entered the monastic order under his paternal uncle, Master Man. By nature, he was exceptionally brilliant and far surpassed others; once the *Lotus Sūtra* was taught to him, he could recite it from memory as soon as the instruction ceased.

At the age of sixteen, he received full ordination and maintained the Vinaya precepts without slackening. Feeling a profound resolve for the Great Dharma, he traveled to Ningbo to rely upon Master Quan of Ban-shan.

He practiced the *Tiantai* *Zhi-guan* and specialized in the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* and Pure Land repentance rituals. During his meditative concentration (*samādhi*), he had a vision of the Venerable Mañjuśrī holding a rhinoceros-horn *cintāmaṇi*.

From that time on, his eloquence increased daily. He propagated the Dharma throughout Eastern Wu and the two provinces of Zhejiang, regarding the circulation of the teachings as his primary objective.
He established one hundred and ten assemblies for the *Lotus Sūtra*, frequently receiving the auspicious sign of celestial flowers.

This was an auspicious omen. When the coast at Yanguan collapsed, he was requested to perform a great Water and Land Assembly (*shuilu dahui*). The Master focused his mind in contemplation, took sand from the sea, and consecrated it with mantras.
He scattered it everywhere across the site; wherever his footprints reached, the shore did not collapse. This occurred in the seventh year of the Zhizheng era.
He summoned the assembly and entrusted them with the teaching that the Pure Land is mind-only. Sitting upright, he wrote a verse and passed away.

Yuan Chen Junzhang was a native of Huangyan. He was dignified and spoke little. At the age of forty, together with his wife, Lady Ye, he recited the *Lotus Sūtra* and practiced mindfulness of the Buddha with great diligence.
At sixty, when his illness became critical, one night he ordered his son, Jingxing, to support him.
He sat down and said, "I am returning. [The others] asked, "Where are you going? He replied, "I am going to the place of extinction.
Again he said, "When I die, you should follow the *śramaṇa* method of cremation (*jāva*). Having finished speaking, he joined his palms, recited "Namo Amitābha Buddha," and passed away.

Shi Shanji, style name Haihui, of Nengren Temple on Mount Tiantai, was a native of Zhuji. When he was barely able to speak, he heard his mother reciting the Buddha’s name and immediately joined his palms, chanting along with her voice.
At the age of ten, he received the tonsure at Lingmi Temple in Shanyin and followed Master Da-shan Huai to study the teachings and contemplations of the Tiantai school.
Later, he received the Dharma from Master Zantang Cheng and served as the abbot of three famous temples.
Lan Hongchan expounded the *Fahua xuanyi* and *Wenju*. Teaching in the morning and interpreting in the evening, he clarified the profound meanings through his five chapters and four exegeses.

During one of his lecture periods, he was moved by a dream in which the Venerable Ziming appeared to him. In his later years, he lived in seclusion at Huajing, where he strictly cultivated the practices of the Pure Land.
Throughout his life, the Master lectured on the *Lotus Sūtra* and the *Prabhūtaratna Sūtra*, and he took the *Lotus Sūtra* and *Pure Land Repentance Ritual* as his primary practice.
The manifestations of his spiritual wonders were manifold.
This was the Great Master Lianchi (Huzhong), whose secular surname was Shen of the ancient city of Hangzhou; he resided at Yunqi Temple on Mount Wuyun.

Having set his mind upon the Buddha-vehicle in his early twenties, in the Bingyin year of the Jiajing era, he received the tonsure under Wumen Xingtian and subsequently received full ordination. He practiced alone...
Carrying only a gourd and a single sandal, he traveled extensively to consult various masters. While traveling north to Mount Wutai, he was moved by Manjusri’s manifestation of light.

In the *Xinwei* year of the Longqing era, seeing that the mountains and waters of Yunqi were secluded and serene, he settled there, building a thatched hut to spend the remainder of his life. The area surrounding the mountain suffered frequently from tiger disasters; the Master recited scriptures for them on their behalf.

After he performed the rite of offering food to the hungry ghosts, the tiger’s affliction was pacified. During a year of drought, he walked through the fields while reciting the Buddha’s name; wherever his feet reached, timely rain fell in profusion.

From this point on, his path of transformation flourished greatly. The Master alone pioneered the single gate of the Pure Land, synthesizing the Tripitaka and pointing toward the mind-only as the ultimate destination.
Monastics and laypeople from all quarters who prostrated themselves before his lotus pedestal numbered several thousand per day, including various worthies, nobles, and—

Inquirers came to his gate in constant succession; all of them struck the key points and beat the rhythm of the teachings, seeking to investigate the Great Matter, none of whom failed to have their minds humbled.
Furthermore, with the utmost sincerity and compassion, he composed the "Essay on Prohibiting Killing and Releasing Living Beings" to exhort the world.

Both within and outside the city, as well as in the mountains, he established ponds for releasing living beings, saving countless lives of fish and birds every year. During the Wanli era, Empress Dowager Cisheng...
Later, the Emperor dispatched an inner attendant to deliver a purple *kāṣāya* robe, offerings for a vegetarian feast, and inquiries regarding the essentials of the Dharma.

Those throughout the land who heard the Master’s name unanimously declared, "Yunqi is an ancient Buddha. The Master secretly cultivated the Four Practices of Peaceful Bliss (*catur-ānanda-caryā*) and bore the True Dharma upon his shoulders;

his esoteric conduct was difficult to fathom. By means of the *nienfo* samādhi, he universally gathered in practitioners of the three capacities. Truly, he was the one peer since the time of Yongming. —Hanshan.
The Zen Master composed an inscription for his stupa, saying: "Were it not for the formal entrustment, this would surely have been a manifestation emerging from the earth.

Thus, those who truly knew the Master were few indeed. The Master once wrote a eulogy for the embroidered *Lotus Sūtra*, which says: "Within forty-nine years, he revealed the Buddha’s knowledge and vision;
having attained this upon the tip of a single hair, it manifests within all atoms of dust. While others employ brush and ink, you instead use needle and thread. [Leaf]
The lotus leaf is born from the Dharma; every syllable radiates light everywhere. The nature of the mind is fundamentally formless, yet it can transform according to conditions.
Taking my pen as my tongue, I now offer this as a memorial. May we together forge the karmic bond of Bodhi, forever turning the wheel of Dharma within the Palace of the Empty King.
Furthermore, there was once a lotus leaf inscribed with verses from a commentary on a sutra, recorded in the *Yunqi Fahui*.
Master Ming Shi Deqing was a native of Quanpao. His secular surname was Cai. At the age of nine, he was able to recite the *Pumenpin* (Universal Gate Chapter).

At twelve, his teacher instructed him in the *Lotus Sūtra*, which he mastered through recitation in three months. At twenty, he practiced Chan meditation, dedicating himself with intense resolve to its investigation.

He traveled to the capital, where he visited Master An to study the *Lotus Sūtra* and the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi*. Thereafter, he traveled to Qingliang Mountain and reached Mount Hanshan at Beitaishan, where he took delight in its extraordinary beauty.
